one_line: Chaulukya king Bhima I and his guild of sthapatis designing the Sun Temple of Modhera as a cosmic, hydraulic and solar-engineering marvel.

appearance.age_look: Bhima I: late 30s to early 40s, tall and broad-shouldered; chief sthapati: mid-40s, lean and wiry; junior sthapati: mid-20s, compact build.
appearance.face: Bhima I has an oval face, medium warm-brown complexion, straight nose, neatly trimmed moustache, strong jaw and calm, observant eyes with a composed, authoritative default expression; chief sthapati has a slightly angular face, sun-weathered medium-brown skin, fine lines at the eyes, a short boxed beard and an intense, thoughtful gaze; junior sthapati has a softer oval face, smooth medium-brown complexion, no facial hair and a curious, focused expression.
appearance.hair: Bhima I’s black hair is medium-length, combed back and tied into a low knot under a plain conical golden crown with a narrow band and small central sun emblem; chief sthapati’s black hair is pulled into a short, tidy topknot with a white cotton headband tied around the forehead; junior sthapati’s black hair is shoulder-length, straight and tied back in a low ponytail with a simple cord, no headwear.
appearance.costume: Bhima I wears a rich saffron-yellow silk angarakha-style upper garment with three-quarter sleeves and wrap-front knot at the right side, bordered with a narrow maroon band and tiny woven sun motifs, over a deep maroon silk dhoti wrapped in the Western Indian style, pleated in front and tied at the waist with a gold-threaded sash, plus a light cream cotton uttariya draped from the left shoulder across the chest and around the back; he has a sturdy brown leather belt holding a small dagger sheath, simple gold kadas on both wrists, a discreet gold chain with a small sun-shaped pendant, and brown leather sandals. The chief sthapati wears an unbleached off-white cotton angarkha with full sleeves, knee-length and simply cut, tied with cloth ties on the right, over a dull-ochre cotton dhoti with thin dark-red stripes, tied high at the waist, and a plain brown cotton kamarband; he has a long, narrow, faded indigo cotton uttariya draped scarf-like around the shoulders, bare feet with dusted soles, a simple wooden bead necklace and a copper bangle on his right wrist. The junior sthapati wears a light grey-blue cotton kurta with three-quarter sleeves and side slits to mid-thigh, over a soft cream cotton dhoti tied shorter for ease of movement, held with a dark-brown cloth belt, plus a short, sleeveless dark-olive cotton waistcoat; he is barefoot, with a thin cord bracelet on the left wrist and a small cloth pouch tied at his belt.
appearance.signature: Bhima I holds a rolled palm-leaf manuscript tied with a red cord in his left hand and rests his right hand on the hilt of a sheathed short khanda at his waist, while the chief sthapati carries a long wooden measuring staff marked with notches and a simple plumb bob hanging from his belt, and the junior sthapati holds a flat wooden board bearing a carved miniature layout of the Modhera complex showing the stepped kunda, sabhamandapa and sanctum aligned on a solar axis.

ref_desc: Bhima I is a broad-shouldered, medium-brown man with a low-knotted black hairstyle under a simple golden sun-crown, saffron angarakha, maroon dhoti, cream uttariya, leather belt and sandals, holding a palm-leaf roll and sheathed khanda, flanked by two modestly dressed cotton-clad sthapatis with headband and topknot or ponytail, one bearing a notched measuring staff and the other a wooden model of the Modhera temple complex, all in saffron, maroon, cream, indigo and off-white tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of three fixed characters together: Bhima I in the centre as a tall, broad-shouldered Chaulukya king with medium-brown complexion, oval face, neat moustache and calm gaze, black hair combed back into a low knot beneath a plain conical golden crown with a small central sun emblem; dress him in a saffron-yellow silk angarakha with three-quarter sleeves and maroon-edged borders with tiny sun motifs, a deep maroon silk dhoti wrapped in Western Indian style and pleated in front, a gold-threaded waist sash, a light cream uttariya draped from his left shoulder across his chest, simple gold wrist kadas, a subtle gold sun pendant, a brown leather belt with a sheathed short khanda and brown leather sandals, one hand resting on the khanda hilt and the other holding a rolled palm-leaf manuscript tied with a red cord. On his right, show the chief sthapati as a mid-40s, lean, medium-brown man with an angular, sun-worn face, short boxed beard, intense eyes, and black hair in a tidy topknot wrapped with a white cotton headband; dress him in an off-white cotton angarkha with full sleeves, knee-length, over a dull-ochre striped cotton dhoti, brown cloth kamarband, a faded indigo uttariya around his shoulders, bare feet, wooden bead necklace, copper wrist bangle, carrying a long wooden measuring staff with visible notches and a simple plumb bob hanging from his belt. On Bhima’s left, draw the junior sthapati as a compact, mid-20s man with a soft oval face, smooth medium-brown complexion, curious expression and black hair tied back in a low ponytail; clothe him in a light grey-blue cotton kurta with three-quarter sleeves and side slits, a cream cotton dhoti tied shorter for movement with a dark-brown cloth belt, a dark-olive sleeveless waistcoat, thin cord bracelet, a small cloth pouch at his belt, barefoot, holding a flat wooden board displaying a carved miniature plan of the Modhera Sun Temple complex with stepped kunda, sabhamandapa and aligned sanctum; keep all garments modest and fully covering, and use a colour palette dominated by saffron yellow, deep maroon, cream, indigo and off-white, with consistent face shapes, hairstyles, costumes and props clearly visible.
